input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale: No usage, licence or fee-verification audit right binds Customer anywhere in this Agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records" and "monitor" return nothing relevant, and §§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning) and 13.2 (Acceptable Use Policy) give IBM no monitoring or verification rights. § 11.3 is an acceptable-use enforcement right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the Content/AUP warranty in § 11.2(b) and then remove Content, restrict access or terminate. It grants no access to Customer systems or records for measuring our usage or charges, so the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, underpayment true-up) do not attach to it. Because the complete absence of an audit right is better than the preferred position and benefits Bluefly, the playbook direction rule means this is compliant rather than "missing" or a deviation, and no redline or comment is warranted. On the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check: the miss is expected here, since there is no audit clause capable of carrying a frequency cap, and it is not evidence of an unmet playbook position. Noted for the file only, not as deviations: § 11.3 does not bind investigators to confidentiality or expressly exclude access to Customer systems, and the p0137 notice is best-efforts and attaches only to restriction/removal actions; if § 11.3 is reopened for other reasons we could seek notice where practicable, investigator confidentiality and no access to our systems beyond what is necessary. The suspension and termination remedies in § 11.3(a)-(d) are left to the suspension and termination rules to avoid double-flagging.
